options: It proves a broader claim that the passage never establishes.
It ignores an important condition stated in the passage.
It treats an estimate as if it were a verified fact.
The described pattern is more credible if it remains consistent when conditions are comparable.
It compares the two cases without controlling for a relevant difference.

questions.question: How would the interpretation change if the missing condition were reversed? Read this context first: A character makes a decision based on incomplete information. options: It reverses the relationship described by the writer.
It describes a possibility rather than an established conclusion.
It confuses the writer’s opinion with the reported evidence.
Changing the key condition would require the reader to reassess the original interpretation.
It proves a broader claim that the passage never establishes.
